slides.title: The language of motion
slides.lede: Opener: three scenes, seven questions, answered on your boards

slides.title: The Toy Car
slides.alt: A toy car on a straight track, drawn large

slides.title: A toy car on a straight track

setup.preamble: A toy car is in motion along a straight line. A strobe light leaves a dot at the car's position on each flash, which makes a motion diagram.
setup.para: The displacement $s$ of the car is its position relative to a fixed origin $O$: $s>0$ is right of $O$ and $s<0$ is left. At $t=0$ the car is $4$ m left of $O$ and speeding up. The strobe flashes every second.

facts.html: Displacement $s$ is the position relative to the origin $O$
$s>0$ is right of $O$, $s<0$ is left; $s$ in metres, $t$ in seconds
At $t=0$ the car is at $s=-4$ m
The strobe leaves one dot every second

scene.alt: A toy car on a straight track above the graph of position against time

slides.title: Left or right?
slides.stem: The car has been moving for $1$ second. Which side of $O$ is it on, and which way is it moving?

walk.note: When $s(t)<0$, the car is to the left of $O$.
The dots move right and the graph of $s$ rises, so the car is moving to the right.

scene.alt: A toy car on a straight track above the graph of position against time

slides.title: Where is the next dot? (1 of 2)
slides.stem: The gaps between the dots are growing. What does that say about $v$, and what is the sign of $a$? Where will the next dot be?

walk.note: The car covers more distance each second.
The signs of $v$ and $a$ are the same, so the speed is increasing.

scene.alt: A toy car on a straight track above the graph of position against time

slides.title: Where is the next dot? (2 of 2)
slides.stem: Where will the next dot be?

walk.note: The gaps grow by $1$ m each second.

scene.alt: A toy car on a straight track above the graph of position against time

slides.title: Turning Round
slides.alt: A toy car on a straight track, drawn large

setup.preamble: The toy car is back at the start of the track. This time it does not keep going the same way.
setup.para: At $t=0$ the car is at $O$ and moving to the right. It slows down, comes to rest for an instant, and reverses direction. The strobe still flashes once every second. Dots made while the car moves back are drawn on a second row, so none are hidden.

facts.html: Displacement $s$ is the position relative to the origin $O$
The car starts at $O$, moving to the right
The strobe leaves one dot every second
Dots made while it moves back drop to a second row

scene.alt: A toy car on a straight track above the graph of position against time

slides.title: At rest (1 of 2)
slides.stem: At $t=3$ the car is instantaneously at rest, at its furthest point from $O$. What is $v$ there, and what is $a$?

walk.note: The car is instantaneously at rest, and the sign of $v$ changes.
The velocity falls by $2\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ each second.

scene.alt: A toy car on a straight track above the graph of position against time

walk.note: It is not zero at rest: $v$ is still changing.

scene.alt: A toy car on a straight track above the graph of position against time

slides.title: Distance and displacement
slides.stem: At $t=6$ the car is back at $O$. What is the distance travelled, and what is the change in displacement?

walk.note: Distance accumulates whichever way the car travels.
The change in displacement ignores the detour.

scene.alt: A toy car on a straight track above the graph of position against time

slides.title: Michael's Ride
slides.alt: A cyclist on a hill drawn as he rides,, drawn large

setup.preamble: Michael rides up a hill and down the other side to his friend's house. The dots show his position at various times $t$.
setup.para: His position along the road, measured from the start, is $s(t)=1.2t^3-30t^2+285t$ metres, for $0\le t\le 19$ minutes. He never rides backward, so $s$ is also the distance he has travelled. The hill is drawn only as he rides, so its steepness is not visible ahead of him. The picture is a sketch, not to scale.

facts.html: $s$ is measured from the start, in metres; $t$ is in minutes, $0\le t\le 19$
At $t=0$ he is at the start, $s=0$
The dots show his position every minute

scene.alt: A cyclist on a hill drawn as he rides, above the graph of distance against time

slides.title: The steepest part
slides.stem: Michael has ridden for $12$ minutes. At what point do you think the hill was steepest? How far had Michael travelled to this point?

walk.note: The closest dots are between $t=8$ and $t=9$: he rides slowest there, so the hill is steepest.
Slowest is $35\ \text{m min}^{-1}$ at $t=\tfrac{25}{3}$, where $s=\tfrac{8875}{9}$ m.

scene.alt: A cyclist on a hill drawn as he rides, above the graph of distance against time

slides.title: Average speed
slides.stem: How can we find Michael's average speed between $t=5$ and $t=15$ minutes? Find it.

walk.note: Also his distance, as he never goes back.
It is the gradient of the chord through the two points.

scene.alt: A cyclist on a hill drawn as he rides, above the graph of distance against time

slides.title: Speed at an instant (1 of 2)
slides.stem: How can we find Michael's speed at a particular instant? Estimate it at $t=10$.

walk.note: The chord over a short interval around $t=10$.
The values approach $45$ as the chord becomes the tangent.

scene.alt: A cyclist on a hill drawn as he rides, above the graph of distance against time

walk.note: The instantaneous speed is the gradient of the tangent. Worked Example 1 in the notes starts here.

scene.alt: A cyclist on a hill drawn as he rides, above the graph of distance against time
